explanation: Mathlib's Fermat-type results in Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/LocalExtr/Basic.lean are general: IsLocalMinOn.hasFDerivWithinAt_nonneg / IsLocalMaxOn.hasFDerivWithinAt_nonpos hold for directions in the positive tangent cone. Deriving the one-sided statement from them means proving -1 ∈ posTangentConeAt (Set.Iic a) a (a segment argument) and converting between HasDerivWithinAt and HasFDerivWithinAt. That is more than routine glue. I searched Mathlib for one-sided specialisations: IsLocalMinOn/IsLocalMaxOn together with Iic/Ici/Iio/Ioi, names like *_Iic_nonpos / *_Iic_nonneg / *_Ici_*, and posTangentConeAt membership lemmas for intervals. Mathlib has only the general one_mem_posTangentConeAt_iff_* lemmas and the ad hoc Icc uses in Darboux.lean. No direct match was found. The library's proof uses its own companion lemma (the IsLocalMaxOn version, applied to -f).
